transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Elliot Park (Novus CTO), Maya Chen (Infra Lead), Samir Patel (Security)

Summary:
- Novus evaluating Private/VPC deployment vs Hosted/Dedicated; primary concerns: network topology, VPC peering or PrivateLink, region constraints (EU residency), and security/KMS.
- Next: send security docs, share VPC diagram, schedule SE-led deep dive/benchmarks, pricing for dedicated pilot.

Topics: VPC peering vs Private endpoints; region residency (eu-west-1 requirement); KMS/HSM integration; SSO and RBAC; latency SLO; dedicated pool sizing and autoscale; fallback to hosted.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, um quick intro I'm Jordan from Redwood the AE on the account and with me is Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Elliot: cool thanks, yeah I'm Elliot CTO at Novus, with Maya infra and Samir security.
[00:18] Priya: nice to meet you all, we'll focus on your private/vpc constraints and how Redwood can fit into your infra.
[00:25] Maya: great, quick context: we're building a gen-ai platform for enterprise customers and we have strict data residency and network isolation requirements, so hosted public internet endpoints are a non-starter for some customers.
[00:36] Samir: and from security we're focused on encryption keys, audit logs, and SSO integration, also need to know what logs are captured and retention.
[00:46] Jordan: totally makes sense. high-level question - are you thinking dedicated reserved capacity (our Dedicated offering) or full Private deployment in your VPC? or both as an option?
[00:58] Elliot: we were leaning Private in our VPC so we control egress and peering. dedicated is interesting if the cost/throughput tradeoffs are better but private is the must-have for regulated customers.
[01:12] Priya: ok good. on Private we offer two main connectivity patterns: VPC peering / transit gateway peering for cross-account routing, and PrivateLink-style private endpoints (we call them private endpoints) so you don't have to route over the public internet. which would you prefer?
[01:30] Maya: peering is our default but we use AWS Transit Gateway in main account; we want to avoid transitive routing headaches. also some customers require us to keep workloads in eu-west-1, is Redwood able to deploy in eu-west-1?
[01:43] Jordan: yes we have private region options in eu-west-1 for Private deployments; for Dedicated we also have capacity in eu-west-1 depending on commitment. one note - if you require in-region key management we can integrate with your KMS or HSM via customer-managed keys.
[01:58] Samir: integration with our KMS is critical. how do you handle keys at rest and in transit? what about audit trail?
[02:06] Priya: keys at rest: we can either use customer-managed KMS in your account (we don't hold plaintext keys) or use a dedicated HSM integration. in transit is TLS, and we push audit logs to your logging endpoints - either CloudWatch or a syslog sink; retention is configurable but we'll capture token-level cost and latency traces in the console.
[02:25] Elliot: ok sounds good. can you talk about the networking details - IP ranges, NAT, and how we'd set up peering to avoid port conflicts? we have strict CIDR blocks.
[02:36] Priya: from the Redwood side we'll provide an expected egress IP set for the Private deployment; typically we ask customers to allocate a /24 or multiple /24s depending on scale. if peering via Transit Gateway we can route directly and avoid NAT, but if using PrivateLink we'll provision interface endpoints in your VPC and you connect via ENIs - that reduces blast radius but requires endpoint quotas.
[02:58] Maya: endpoint quotas are a thing; we might have to request increases. also wondering about cross-region fallback - if we deploy in eu-west-1 but there's outage, what's the fallback? we can't move data out of region.
[03:11] Jordan: if data residency is mandatory for a workload, our automated fallback won't move it out of region. we can configure regional fallbacks to another eu region if policy allows, otherwise we fail closed and service degrade gracefully. for multi-region resilient setups you typically replicate or deploy redundant Private clusters in each permitted region.
[03:31] Samir: and what about SSO? we use SAML-based IdP, and need RBAC for team-level access.
[03:36] Priya: we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; role-based access is available in our Private control plane, and you can map roles to your IdP groups. audit logs of user actions are exportable to your SIEM.
[03:50] Elliot: latency is a big piece for our interactive product - targets are p95 <200ms for short prompts and bulk batch for embeddings. how does Private compare latency-wise to Hosted?
[04:02] Priya: Private in your VPC will eliminate the internet hop so typically you see ~20-40ms lower p95 compared to our hosted public endpoints, depending on where your app lives. Dedicated in our network with peering also performs well, but private in-region is usually best for latency. caching and prefix KV caching also help with repeated requests.
[04:22] Maya: good - can you support autoscaling? we have bursty traffic.
[04:26] Jordan: yes Dedicated has autoscale and reserved pools; Private we can set autoscaling policies too but typically that's coordinated with your infra team because it may involve spinning up downstream capacity in your VPC. we can do a burst policy with Redwood-managed GPUs if you want a hybrid fallback to avoid cold start.
[04:43] Elliot: cost - what's the delta between Dedicated and Private? any hidden network egress?
[04:48] Priya: Private often has higher baseline platform fees because we're hosting a control plane in your VPC and managing connectors; network egress depends on traffic patterns but for in-region traffic you should avoid egress charges if everything stays in-region. Dedicated is simpler if you want Redwood-managed infra without VPC ownership, and can be cheaper at high sustained usage. we'll send a pricing matrix.
[05:08] Samir: any compliance docs? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[05:11] Jordan: yes - SOC2 report, ISO summary, and our penetration test summary. we'll share redacted reports; for Private we can also support customer-specific audit scopes in enterprise engagements.
[05:22] Maya: network question - do you support VPC peering via account-to-account, or only via Transit Gateway? we prefer TGW for cross-account routing.
[05:30] Priya: both. we can peer account-to-account for simpler setups or integrate with Transit Gateway for central routing. for large enterprises TGW is the recommended pattern. there can be routing table management overhead but we provide IaC templates (Terraform) to wire it up.
[05:46] Elliot: ok that helps. can you send Terraform examples?
[05:49] Jordan: yep will share the repo link and a starter template.
[05:52] Maya: what about IP allowlists - some customers want only specific IPs to talk to endpoints.
[05:58] Priya: with Private endpoints you can control security groups and NACLs on the interface endpoints; with peering you control route tables and security groups. we also support TLS client certs for mutual TLS if you want extra assurance.
[06:12] Samir: curious about model variants - we use some local distilled models for latency and fallback to larger models for quality; can Redwood host multiple model versions and route based on policy?
[06:22] Priya: yes model cataloging, version pinning, and rollout policies are first-class. you can route by latency, cost, or quality, and we support automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants. also we have Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching to reduce token cost.
[06:40] Elliot: great. any gotchas around private endpoints and IPv6?
[06:44] Priya: currently primary support is IPv4 for interface endpoints, IPv6 support is coming but not GA for all regions - we'll note that for eu-west-1.
[06:56] Maya: ok, logistics - what do you need from us to spin up a demo/private pilot?
[07:01] Jordan: ideally: a VPC CIDR set, whether you'll use TGW or do account peering, KMS key ARN if you want CMK integration, and a set of sample workloads/traffic patterns for Priya to run benchmarks. also decide which region(s) we should provision in.
[07:18] Maya: we can provide CIDR and TGW intent. one question - how long does provisioning take?
[07:22] Priya: for a simple Private endpoint demo we can do it in a few days once we have the infra details and IP allocations; full Private cluster with dedicated nodes and HSM integration is closer to 2-4 weeks depending on legal/compliance paperwork.
[07:36] Elliot: that's acceptable. any demo data security concerns? we will want to scrub PII from sample prompts but low-level logs will be safe in our test VPC.
[07:47] Samir: also need to know about log retention and ability to purge logs for specific workloads.
[07:52] Priya: we can configure retention and support purge workflows; for enterprise we can arrange specific retention policies and data deletion proofs.
[08:02] Jordan: cool, next steps recap: we'll send SOC2 and security whitepaper, Terraform templates, VPC peering examples, and pricing for a Dedicated vs Private pilot. Priya will scope the infra and benchmark plan. Maya will send CIDR and TGW details.
[08:18] Elliot: sounds good.
[08:20] Maya: one last tangential thing - does Redwood support running the control plane in our account fully air-gapped? we have one customer with that requirement.
[08:31] Priya: yes we offer Private on-prem or fully customer-managed control plane for very large regulated customers; that's a separate enterprise project with longer lead times but supported.
[08:43] Samir: ok nice. thanks all.
[08:45] Jordan: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling links.
[08:48] End meeting.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (k-v cache transcribed as k v cash in places), speaker timestamps approximate.
